ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Duke Kahanamoku — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Two-week review: echocardiogram, heart failure cardiology consultation the same day, the diagnosis, and guideline-directed medicines

text.paragraph: Two-week review: echocardiogram, heart failure consultation and the diagnosis. [S]

Mr. Kahanamoku returns two weeks after intake and is seen the same day by Dr. Abernathy-Chen of heart failure cardiology after his echocardiogram this morning. At his wish, two members of his ʻohana joined the discussion with the cardiologist. On furosemide 40 mg he has lost 2.6 kg; his ankles swell less, and he now sleeps on one pillow. He is still breathless walking up a slope and has not been back in the water. He has had no chest pain, palpitations, fainting or lightheadedness. He took his last lisinopril dose this morning. The echocardiogram shows a weak heart muscle with an ejection fraction of 30% and an old scar at the front and tip of the heart. [S]

list.item:
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction from ischemic cardiomyopathy, NYHA class III (I50.22). Breathlessness, ankle swelling, NT-proBNP 2,450 pg/mL and an ejection fraction of 30% with a thinned, akinetic anterior wall and apex establish HFrEF from an old anterior infarction. Less congested on furosemide. Potassium 3.9 mmol/L and creatinine 1.08 mg/dL (eGFR 76) two weeks after furosemide. Dr. Abernathy-Chen agrees and advises starting all four medicine classes within weeks. [S]
Stop lisinopril (last dose this morning); start sacubitril-valsartan 24/26 mg twice daily 36 hours after that dose.
Stop metoprolol tartrate; start carvedilol 3.125 mg twice daily with food this evening.
Start empagliflozin 10 mg daily, with sick-day rules.
Continue furosemide 40 mg daily and daily weights.
Spironolactone at the next visit if potassium and kidney function allow.
Metabolic panel in two weeks.

Iron deficiency without anemia (E61.1). Ferritin 62 ng/mL and transferrin saturation 16% in HFrEF: intravenous iron improves symptoms and exercise capacity. [S]
Ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg intravenously today, and again in two weeks.

Coronary artery disease with an old anterior infarction (I25.2). No angina. A new reduction in heart function needs an ischemic evaluation. [S]
Coronary angiography next week.
Continue aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 80 mg.

Follow-up: Coronary angiography next week. Review in two weeks with a metabolic panel, the KCCQ-12 and the second iron infusion. Call for a weight gain of more than 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week, lightheadedness, or breathlessness at rest; call 911 for chest pain or fainting. Next scheduled visit 1957-04-13: two-week review after sacubitril-valsartan, carvedilol and empagliflozin: kidney function, potassium, angiography result and the next medicine. [S]
